notes: Chapter 1.3.1 places the user two to four metres from the phone, side on, wearing
headphones. In that position the user cannot read the screen and, on the target
device, cannot see it at all: 4.1 points the rear cameras at the user, which
puts the main display face down the other way. Speech is therefore not an
enhancement of the interface before a set. It is the interface.
These lines are the ones that do not belong to any one exercise: acknowledgements
and rejections, which read the same whatever is being trained. The lines that do
belong to an exercise stay in that exercise's specification, as framing.guidance
and as each calibration measure's instruction, and name their asset there.
Every line here is spoken before Stage.SET and never during it. From the first
repetition onward the cue bank owns the audio channel, because NFR-P1 is measured
through it and a second speaker in that window is a second thing to attend to.
Wording rule: short, and an instruction rather than a status. 'Step back' tells
the user what to do; 'framing failed' tells them what the software thinks.
One line per transition, never two. SoundPool mixes rather than queues, so a
spoken acknowledgement followed immediately by the next instruction would be two
voices at once. There is nothing to acknowledge separately in any case: being
asked for the next hold is how the user learns the last one was accepted, and a
rejection line already says that the hold is about to be repeated. Drafts of this
file carried FRAMED and ACCEPTED lines; both were cut for exactly this reason.

en.text: Set started. Walk back, and begin when you are ready.
